title: Generalizable Recommender System During Temporal Popularity Distribution Shifts

problem.claim: Popularity-influenced embeddings may perform poorly when test-time popularity distributions differ from historical distributions.

gap.claim: Existing disentangled embedding methods often overlook the temporal nature of popularity shifts during training and inference.

contributions.claim: TPAB is a disentanglement framework that incorporates temporal popularity.
TPAB introduces temporal-aware user and item embeddings, popularity coarsening, and popularity bootstrapping.
The paper provides theoretical analysis of the bootstrapping loss.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe TPAB as a novel disentanglement framework incorporating temporal popularity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the bootstrapping loss eliminates the effect of popularity on the learned model.
The authors report extensive experiments on real-world datasets validating TPAB.
The authors report outstanding generalization ability during temporal popularity distribution shifts.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems rely on user and item attribute embeddings for accurate recommendations.
Entangled embeddings combine intrinsic property and popularity factors, creating challenges under changed popularity distributions.
Existing disentanglement remedies address popularity shifts but often omit their temporal nature.
TPAB addresses the gap with temporal-aware embeddings, popularity coarsening, and popularity bootstrapping.
The authors report theoretical analysis, test-time popularity inference, and experiments on real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: Popularity distribution can influence learned embeddings and create difficulties when the distribution changes at test time.

interpretation.claim: Distribution-shift robustness may require separating stable property factors from changing popularity factors.

application.claim: For recommender systems, model popularity as a distinct and temporally changing component during training and inference.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that temporal disentanglement is necessary for all recommender systems or shift settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, evaluation metrics, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the temporal-aware embedding architecture or training procedure in detail.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical assumptions or proof.
